products.name: Epic AI (SlicerDicer, etc.)
products.note: Clinical decision support; patient data exposure; HIPAA critical; FDA SaMD considerations

reading.body:
Epic Systems embeds AI into clinical workflows and patient interfaces across its healthcare software platform, with tools for documentation, decision support, and patient engagement integrated into products serving hospitals and practices.

The company's AI deployment sits at a critical juncture: healthcare facilities depend on Epic's systems to manage patient data at scale, and adding AI to those systems means clinical decision support, documentation assistance, and patient-facing chat interfaces now operate on patient records in real time. This integration means Epic's computational load grows with AI adoption across its installed base. The regulatory surface area is substantial. Patient data exposure and HIPAA compliance are inherent to the architecture, not bolt-on concerns. FDA software-as-a-medical-device classification adds another layer of constraint on what changes the company can ship and how quickly.

The data covers Epic's AI products and regulatory considerations but does not address the compute infrastructure required to run these systems, whether Epic operates its own data centers or relies on cloud providers, or what power and cooling demands this workload creates. It also does not indicate whether these AI features are available to all customers or represent capacity-constrained rollouts. For understanding how healthcare AI scales within the broader constraint model, the infrastructure underlying these products remains opaque.

profile_text.body:
Epic Systems is a healthcare software company founded in 1979, according to its website, and headquartered in Verona. The company describes its purpose as developing software to help people get well, stay well, and help future generations be healthier, and notes it was founded in a basement in 1979.

Its AI work centers on tools built directly into Epic. The company says clinicians at Memorial Hermann Health System are using an AI tool built into Epic to help patients better understand their test results and make decisions about next steps in their care. It also describes Chart with Art, which it calls Epic's native AI charting, as handling documentation so clinicians can focus on the conversation in the room, and an AI-supported outpatient office visit that helps clinicians arrive prepared, anticipates what they need in the room, and lines up documentation and orders for review before the visit ends. The product tracked here is Epic AI, which includes SlicerDicer, and is noted as clinical decision support involving patient data exposure, HIPAA considerations, and FDA software as a medical device considerations.

No litigation, regulatory filings, or other registry records are held for the company.
